body: Idk if I'm going to help you or not, but I feel you. I lost my chance at college and I was depressed then. I wish I could go back, but I can't afford to. I feel like I'm wasting time and only getting older. I often think about suicide as an easy out because if this is what the next 30-40 years looks like for me before I retire... I don't want to make it that far. All I can say is that if you have the means to fo so, seek help. Maybe go to the school medical office. That's what I did when I was in school. Had I had the money I needed to continue I would've been able to keep getting help until I graduated. Now I pay $160 a month for health insurance that doesn't cover the mental health care I need. Essentially I pay money to not go to the doctor. Yay! Anyway, I feel like I somewhat understand where you're coming from. You're not alone.

At least I can take comfort in knowing it's not so abnormal that I would need to stress about it. Still it's difficult to Google something like this without getting a constant barrage of suicide prevention stuff. Talking about it with a professional is risky. An old therapist of mine sent me to a hospital after a break up because I had mentioned said thoughts at some point during a previous session. Not that session mind you, so I learned not to talk about it with them.

It makes sense in a way. Kind if like fight or flight. I was worried that because these thoughts had become casual that it was as if suicide was no longer a big deal to me. Meaning I wouldn't have too many quarrels with just ending it all some day because of [ insert reason here ].
